chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Umar ibn Udhaynah, from Zurarah, from Abdul Kareem ibn Utbah al-Hashimi, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:

The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) used to distribute the charity of the people of the countryside among the people of the countryside, and the charity of the people of the city among the people of the city, and he did not distribute it between them equally. Rather, he distributed it according to the number of those present from them, and he did not see anything fixed in that.
ai.seo_question: How should zakat be distributed between rural and urban populations according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi clarifies the administrative discretion of the Imam or Caliph in zakat distribution, distinguishing between 'sadaqat al-bawadi' (rural) and 'sadaqat al-hadar' (urban) funds. It establishes that while the source and destination are linked geographically, the distribution is not rigidly fixed per capita but is determined by the Imam's assessment of the number of eligible recipients present at the time. This principle underscores the flexibility of Shia jurisprudence in managing communal wealth based on contemporary needs rather than static formulas.
